ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point A is on the hyperbola $y=\frac{4}{x}$, point B is on the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}$, and $AB\parallel x$-axis, intersecting the y-axis at point C. If $AB=2AC$, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let us draw AD $\perp$ x-axis at D through point A, and draw BE $\perp$ x-axis at E through point B,\\
$\because$ AB $\parallel$ x-axis,\\
$\therefore$ the quadrilateral ACOD is a rectangle, and the quadrilateral BCOE is a rectangle,\\
$\because$ AB = 2AC,\\
$\therefore$ BC = 3AC,\\
$\because$ point A is on the hyperbola $y = \frac{4}{x}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the rectangle ACOD = 4,\\
Similarly, the area of the rectangle BCOE = k,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the rectangle BCOE = $3 \times$ the area of the rectangle ACOD = 12,\\
$\therefore$ k = \boxed{12}
